speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I see you are here to discuss a breast mass. To help me understand your situation, can you tell me how long you have noticed this lump and if it is painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old woman. The patient noticed a mass in her left breast 4 weeks ago, which has rapidly increased in size. She denies any recent trauma or infections. No history of similar complaints in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the rapid growth of this mass over four weeks, have you noticed any skin changes, such as dimpling, redness, or swelling, or any changes to your nipple like inversion or discharge?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Presence of a left breast mass. I also have Rapid increase in size of the mass, No skin or nipple changes, No pain associated with the mass.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is helpful; the rapid growth without skin or nipple changes is notable. Have you experienced any fever, chills, or flu-like symptoms recently? Also, have you had any recent mammograms or breast biopsies?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Phyllodes Tumor

The clinical picture of a rapidly growing, large (6 cm), nontender, multinodular mass in a 48-year-old woman is highly suspicious for a Phyllodes tumor rather than a typical fibroadenoma or carcinoma. While the mammogram and ultrasound images are now requested, do you have any specific family history of breast cancer or known genetic mutations like BRCA1/2?
